definition: Expressive language is the ability to communicate through speech, writing, or signs. In Broca aphasia, this expressive aspect of language is impaired while comprehension is relatively preserved.

provenance.scope: Source record D001039; pinned source text

reasons: The packet’s record is for Broca aphasia, described as an aphasia with impaired expressive language and relatively preserved comprehension; the definition instead defines the general capacity of expressive language and shifts to a condition-specific claim.
The statement about Broca aphasia is not a definition of the term ‘expressive language’ itself, so the requested sense does not match the source record.

The first sentence (“Expressive language is the ability to communicate through speech, writing, or signs.”) is not explicitly stated in the packet; the packet describes expressive language as being impaired (speech, writing, signs) rather than defining it as an ability.
The second sentence about Broca aphasia impairing the expressive aspect while comprehension/receptive abilities are relatively preserved is supported by the packet.
